category: PHP, XML JSON, Laravel, MySQL, JavaScript
title: Session 2: PHP, Laravel, XML/HTML & Environment Fundamentals

questions.questionText: PHP variables must start with a _____.
questions.explanation: In PHP, all variable names must begin with a dollar sign ($), followed by a letter or an underscore (for example, $name or $_count).

questions.questionText:
Which of the following features are true about PHP?
a) Relatively easy for a fresher.
b) Has advanced features for professional programming.
c) Works only on Windows.
questions.explanation: PHP is beginner-friendly (a) and provides advanced object-oriented and server-side features for professional development (b). It is cross-platform and does not work only on Windows.

questions.questionText: What allows users to compile a program into machine code just before it can be executed?
questions.explanation: A JIT (Just-In-Time) compiler compiles program bytecode into native machine code right before execution to improve runtime performance.

questions.questionText: PHP provides __________ function to access the value of all the environment variables.
questions.explanation: PHP's built-in getenv() function returns the value of a specified environment variable or an associative array of all environment variables when called without arguments.

questions.questionText: What are used for storing data such as numeric and character values, strings, and memory addresses?
questions.explanation: Variables are named storage containers used in programming to hold numeric values, characters, strings, and references or memory addresses.

questions.questionText: Which PHP function accepts a variable name as an argument and displays the argument details passed to it?
questions.explanation: var_dump() accepts one or more variables or expressions and outputs structured details including data type, size/length, and value.

questions.questionText: What is the full form of SMTP?
questions.explanation: SMTP stands for Simple Mail Transfer Protocol, the standard protocol used for sending emails across networks.

questions.questionText: In which year was PHP version 8.0 released?
questions.explanation: PHP version 8.0 was officially released in November 2020, introducing the JIT compiler, named arguments, union types, attributes, and match expressions.

questions.questionText: What are the methods by which the data can be submitted to the server for processing? (Select all that apply)
options: Both PHP GET Method and PHP POST Method
questions.correctAnswer: Both PHP GET Method and PHP POST Method
questions.explanation: HTML forms and PHP scripts submit data to the server for processing using both the HTTP GET method ($_GET) and the HTTP POST method ($_POST). PHP DESK and PHP SET are not valid submission methods.

questions.questionText: Which of these are the superglobal variables used to retrieve data from submitted HTML form that have used GET or POST methods? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: In PHP, $_GET retrieves GET form data, $_POST retrieves POST form data, and $_REQUEST aggregates GET, POST, and cookie inputs. $_GETPOST does not exist.

questions.questionText: Which of the following methods is used to retrieve a specific record?
questions.explanation: In Laravel's Eloquent ORM, find() retrieves a single specific record by its primary key (for example, Model::find($id)). all() fetches every record, get() returns a collection of matching records, and retrieve() is not an Eloquent method.

questions.questionText: A _____ in the world of Web and computer networks is a tiny chunk of data carrying information that comes handy and stores user information on local machines.
questions.explanation: An HTTP cookie is a small piece of data sent by a web server and stored locally on the user's machine by the browser to retain state and user information across requests.

questions.questionText: ______ are required to use Composer and Homestead on Windows.
questions.explanation: Composer is a PHP CLI application and requires local PHP binaries (php.exe) on the Windows host operating system to execute and manage Laravel and Homestead setups.

questions.questionText: ______ acts as a version control system for a database that includes many tables.
questions.explanation: In Laravel, migrations act as version control for the database, allowing teams to define, update, and share database table schemas consistently.

questions.questionText: PHP has no support for Unicode, as it only supports a _____-character set.
questions.explanation: In PHP, a string character corresponds to a single byte (8 bits), meaning PHP natively supports a 256-character set and does not have built-in native Unicode support.

questions.questionText: Which of the following directories includes the Views that will be used to display the final Web page as well as the un-compiled assets related to JavaScript and CSS?
questions.explanation: In Laravel, the resources directory contains Blade views (resources/views) along with raw, un-compiled frontend assets such as JavaScript and CSS files.

questions.questionText: ______ help in organizing codes by grouping requests that handle the codes in a single route and class.
questions.explanation: In Laravel's MVC architecture, Controllers organize application code by grouping related HTTP request handlers into a single class instead of keeping all logic in route closures.

questions.questionText: In Laravel convention, ________ are the preferred way to create records, not tables.
questions.explanation: In Laravel's Eloquent ORM convention, models represent database records (for example, Model::create(...) or $model->save()) and are the preferred way to create and manipulate records, whereas database migrations are used to create and alter tables.

questions.questionText: Which of the following enables the user to add elements to the project that follow the Laravel convention?
questions.explanation: Laravel's Artisan CLI (for example, php artisan make:model, make:controller, or make:migration) scaffolds classes and project elements that follow Laravel's built-in naming and structure conventions.

questions.questionText: Which keyword does PHP use to check if an object belongs to a particular class?
questions.explanation: In PHP, the instanceof type operator checks whether an object is an instance of a specific class, inherits from a parent class, or implements an interface.

questions.questionText: _______ automatically assigns routes to all functions that have been declared in the Resource Controller.
questions.explanation: Laravel Resource Routing (Route::resource()) automatically assigns RESTful HTTP routes to standard CRUD actions (index, create, store, show, edit, update, and destroy) declared in a Resource Controller.

questions.questionText: When creating a record, it is necessary to include the _______ keyword array to prevent any malicious attempt.
questions.explanation: In Laravel Eloquent models, the $fillable array acts as an allow-list for mass assignment (such as Model::create($request->all())), preventing attackers from injecting unauthorized column values.

questions.questionText: The GNU License information appears when you install ______.
questions.explanation: Git for Windows (which provides GitBash) is distributed under the GNU General Public License (GPL) and displays the GNU License information screen during setup.

questions.questionText: Using which of the following methods can you select a column name?
questions.explanation: In Laravel's Query Builder and Eloquent ORM, get(['column_name']) accepts an array of column names to select when executing the query (alongside the dedicated select() clause). By contrast, where() filters rows by condition, find() retrieves a single record by primary key, and bigIncrements() defines an auto-incrementing migration column.

questions.questionText: The code 'vagrant@homestead:~$ composer -V' verifies:
questions.explanation: Running 'composer -V' (or 'composer --version') inside the Homestead virtual machine outputs the installed version of Composer.

questions.questionText: What are the major differences between HTML and XML?
options: HTML defines a certain set of tags to be used compulsorily whereas XML does not.
XML is strict about document structure, how it is stored, and transferred, but HTML does not follow these rules.
questions.explanation: HTML uses a fixed set of predefined tags for displaying content and tolerates lenient markup, whereas XML supports custom user-defined tags and enforces strict structural well-formedness for storing and transporting data.
